# Documentation Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that documentation is defined, consistent with behavior, and free of unsupported claims
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Legend**: `[M]` mandatory (a constitution MUST, an approved requirement, or an approved decision); `[O]` optional enhancement or backlog boundary. `G0` is evaluable now against the approved specification, plan, ADRs, and contracts; `G1` is evaluable after `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-analyze`, before implementation. `{Detects: ...}` links an item to a failure pattern in the [README](README.md) detection matrix. Dimension tags: Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Measurability, Coverage, Traceability, Edge Case, Assumption, Conflict, Gap.
## Documentation Set

- [ ] CHK001 - Is the documentation set defined (spec, plan, ADRs, contracts, quickstart or runbook, API change notes, final report) with an owner and location for each? [Completeness, Plan documents table] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the authoritative-source rule defined (ADRs over research.md, contracts over prose)? [Clarity, Spec DEC-106] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is the final report's content defined (built, decisions, test results, limitations, links to evidence) with each claim required to link to evidence? [Measurability, Spec DEC-111, FR-129] [M, G0] {Detects: unsupported-completion-claims}
- [ ] CHK004 - Is the known-limitations content defined in one place (LIM-001..004, R-18, R-19, T-1, untested Node versions)? [Completeness, Spec Known Limitations, Security §6] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK005 - Is a reviewer entry-point document (repository README) defined? [Gap, Constitution X] [M, G0]

## Consistency with Behavior

- [ ] CHK006 - Is it defined that documentation changes with behavior, with a failure when they diverge? [Measurability, POL-TRC-004, Constitution X] [M, G0] {Detects: docs-inconsistent-with-behavior}
- [ ] CHK007 - Must documentation examples validate against schemas, with invented values labelled illustrative? [Coverage, Contracts README CV-03] [M, G0] {Detects: docs-inconsistent-with-behavior}
- [ ] CHK008 - Is the quickstart defined as a target guide whose expected outcomes are marked until executed, so no result is claimed before it exists? [Clarity, Quickstart status] [M, G0] {Detects: unsupported-completion-claims}
- [ ] CHK009 - Are command names, environment variables, and file names consistent across quickstart, ADRs, and plan (docker-compose.yml, APPROVER_CREDENTIAL, evidence paths)? [Consistency, Spec DEC-110..DEC-113] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are spec, plan, contract, and catalogue versions stated and consistent across documents? [Consistency, Spec status, Plan status] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK011 - Do all DEC, ADR, and FR cross-references resolve with no dangling reference? [Traceability, docs/adr, Plan] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the runtime support statement free of overclaiming (tested on Node 24; 20 and 22 declared but untested)? [Clarity, Spec DEC-071] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is API documentation required to be updated for each contract change before release? [Coverage, Change-record schema] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK014 - Are troubleshooting steps defined for stated failure modes (Docker down, Redis down, SAFE_STOPPED)? [Coverage, Quickstart §10] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is the evidence-labelling convention (agent_mode, clock_kind, synthetic, illustrative) documented for readers? [Completeness, Observability §7] [M, G0]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` or `[Conflict]` name a place where the current documents are silent or disagree; they are findings for the reviewer to resolve, not pre-judged results
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially within this file (`CHK001` onward); cite them as `<file>:CHKnnn`
